title: CAN THESE BONES LIVE?
paragraphs: CAN THESE BONES LIVE?
That wasn’t a poetic question.
It was a confrontation.

The valley was not quiet. It was loud with silence.
Sun-bleached skulls. Rib cages split open. Femurs scattered like abandoned swords.
No pulse.
No breath.
No future.
And God walks His prophet right into it.
In Book of Ezekiel 37, the Spirit sets Ezekiel down in the middle of death and asks one question:
“Son of man… can these bones live?”
Pause.

God already knew the answer.
The question wasn’t for information.
It was for revelation.
Ezekiel looks at irreversible loss… and answers carefully:
“O Lord GOD, You know.”

That’s faith under pressure. Not hype. Not denial.
Just surrender.
Let me talk to you straight.
Some of you are standing in a valley right now.

A marriage that feels picked clean.
A calling that dried up.
A prayer that’s been buried so long you stopped visiting the grave.

Dry.
Very dry.
And heaven is asking you the same question.
Can these bones live?
Here’s the tension.

God doesn’t tell Ezekiel to organize the bones.
He doesn’t say, “Strategize. Improve. Network.”
He says:
“Prophesy.”
Speak My Word into what looks impossible.
When Ezekiel obeys, something wild happens.
A rattling.

Bone to bone.
Sinew wrapping structure.
Flesh covering framework.
Skin sealing the miracle.
But they were still not alive.
Structure without Spirit is still a corpse.
Then God commands him again:
“Prophesy to the breath.”
The Hebrew word there is ruach — wind, breath, Spirit.
And when the breath enters?

They stand up.
An exceedingly great army.
From graveyard to army in one chapter.

That’s not self-help.
That’s resurrection power.
Some scholars interpret this vision as primarily about Israel’s national restoration from exile. And yes — historically, that is true. God was promising to bring His people back from Babylon.
But don’t miss the greater echo.
This is the Gospel in shadow form.
Because centuries later, another Son of Man would stand in a valley of death.
His own.
And on the third day, breath would re-enter a pierced body.
Jesus Christ walked out of His grave so your dry bones wouldn’t stay dry.
The same Spirit that raised Christ from the dead is the same Spirit that steps into your valley.
Not to decorate it.
To resurrect it.
What feels dead in your life?

Your purity?
Your courage?
Your first love for God?
Your dream to serve Him?
Bring it into the valley. Don’t hide it.
Then do what Ezekiel did.
Open your mouth.

Speak God’s Word over what shame tried to silence.
Invite the Spirit into what fear declared finished.

Because if Jesus conquered the grave,
your situation is not beyond redemption.

Not the addiction.
Not the betrayal.
Not the wasted years.
What valley are you standing in?
